title: Active-active symmetric failover with per-session hedging and SLO-aware circuit breakers
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Problem: The hosted API edge must support active-active multi-region traffic while preserving streaming session continuity, strict SLOs for tail latency and availability, and graceful degradation when backend capacity or kernel regressions occur. Current failover flows focus on HTTP request handoffs and occasionally drop streaming sessions or replay tokens, which leads to customer-visible truncation and higher error rates.

Goal: Implement a symmetric, per-session hedging & traffic recalibration approach that: (1) maintains 99.95% region-level availability and 99th percentile tail latency within 200ms for short non-stream requests, (2) preserves streaming session continuity (no token loss and graceful resume/rollback semantics), (3) provides SLO-aware circuit-breaking and progressive load-shedding to protect the serving fleet under overload, and (4) supports incremental rollout with observability and clear rollback criteria.

Proposed approach:
- Symmetric hedging: when per-region headroom is uncertain, issue hedged requests to an adjacent region with probabilistic weighting that decays based on observed SLO headroom and KV cache hit confidence.
- Session anchoring and token stitch: introduce a short-lived session anchor record in the metadata plane (ephemeral TTL ~30s) and a token stitch handshake for multi-part streaming sessions so that an active streaming connection can be resumed on another region without token replay or prompt leakage.
- KV cache propagation: compacted KV diffs for recent token/KV cache checkpoints are opportunistically prefetched to candidate failover replicas; hedging includes a small handshake to ensure cache presence before switching.
- SLO-aware circuit breakers: per-route and per-backend breakers use telemetry (p50/p95/p99 latency, CPU/GPU queue length, token per-second) to open progressively; breakers integrate with the hedging weighting function to steer traffic away and enable traffic shaping instead of abrupt cuts.
- Load-shedding policy: define graceful shedding buckets: low-latency non-streams, interactive streams (resumeable), best-effort background jobs. Shedding starts with best-effort and progresses only if SLO headroom remains negative for >30s.
- Safety: require at-most-once visible output guarantees for streaming handoff via an idempotent resume token and a final flush/ack protocol between regions.

Why different from prior designs: this ticket targets symmetric active-active operation where both regions are actively serving, but hedging is used to mask asymmetric transient headroom while preventing session loss through a short-lived anchor + token stitch flow. It balances cost and reliability with telemetry-driven gating rather than static percentage drains.
acceptance_criteria: Canary run for non-streaming routes: 5% hedged traffic to secondary region for 72h with no customer-visible errors and <5% increase in token cost.
Streaming resume test: simulated region failover recovers 95% of active streams within 4s without data duplication using the token-stitch protocol (end-to-end test suite).
SLO-driven breaker: breakers open and close per policy, and hedging weighting responds to p99 latency spikes within 10s during load test.
Performance: p99 latency for short text generation stays <=200ms under 95th percentile load in the canary region configuration.
Observability: dashboards show per-route hedging percentage, session resume success rate, KV cache hit confidence, and an alert that fires when shedding reaches second tier.
Rollback: abort canary and auto-failback to baseline within 30 minutes if the stream resume rate falls below 85% or p99 latency increases by >25%.
Security: no plaintext tokens are logged during handoff; resume tokens encrypted in transit and at rest.
notes: 2025-03-03: Spike completed comparing symmetric hedging vs active-passive drain strategy. Hedging reduced visible tail-error spikes in our synthetic streaming workload (see PR #2281).
2025-03-04: Design review with PM and Observability: requested clearer cost impact metrics and a toggle to disable hedging per-customer (enterprise opt-out).

2025-03-06: Prototype implementation pushed: gateway hedging layer + token-stitch handshake. Early lab tests show resume median 1.2s; edge-case where KV diff >16KB causes extra latency — mitigated by chunked diff transfer. GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/2281

2025-03-07: Load tests against CUDA-backed runtime: observed p99 latency regression of 8% when hedging at 30% for non-streams; we will tune decay constants and only enable hedging for routes with latency sensitivity label set to medium or low. Link to load run: https://dashboard.redwood.internal/runs/hedge-2025-03-07
2025-03-09: Security review request filed for resume tokens and ephemeral anchor TTL handling (SR-556).
2025-03-10: Preparing canary config and rollout playbook; adding telemetry gating and alert thresholds to Console.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Lab: full unit/integration tests for token-stitch and KV diff (done).
Phase 1 - Internal canary: enable hedging on internal traffic only; monitor session resume and p99 latencies for 48h.
Phase 2 - External canary: 1% production traffic for selected non-critical routes + internal streams; 72h observation window.
Phase 3 - Gradual ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% hedged weighting using telemetry gating; monitor cost and resume success.
Phase 4 - Opt-in: enable hedging for eligible tenants with toggle and enterprise opt-out; full rollout when resume rate >=95% and cost delta acceptable.
risk_mitigation: Default hedging weight low (1-5%) for sensitive routes; increase only if headroom signal stabilizes.
Require two independent telemetry signals (latency + queue depth) before advancing shedding tier to avoid flapping.
Automatic circuit breaker rollback if resume success <85% for 10 minutes or p99 latency delta >25%.
Cost monitoring with daily alert if hedging increases token spend by >10% compared to baseline.
